svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 25: the Cave of the Column
svg.text: Entry 25 (VI 1–6) — the Cave of the Column
Schematic plan, north up. One arrangement the text allows; the cave's size and shape and the spacing of its two entrances are not given.
Project reading: a pillar cave fronting east, dig at the northern entrance
Milik 1960 takes “facing east” with the cave as a whole; “northern” picks the northern of
the two mouths, not a north-facing one (entry25_direction_review).
Project reading (Puech pillar; Milik's eastward cave)
the cave faces east · הצופא מזרח
Milik: the cave as a whole, not each mouth
dig 3 cubits ≈ 1.5 m: a jar, one scroll,
Section at the northern entrance (schematic), west to the left
Down from the northern threshold, whose
The jar holds one scroll; the 42 talents
A stricter project model than Milik's; the singular הצופא
after plural “entrances” does not settle it.
Both openings in an east wall,
Variant: a terrace, not a pillar
Puech p. 60 records Allegro's “platform or terrace”;
such a cave need have no pillar between the mouths.
Deposit: under the jar, or under the scroll
“Under it” can refer to the jar or to the scroll inside it;
Puech prefers under the jar. Both kept (puech_entry25).
Three cubits: a depth or a distance?
Vertical: down from the threshold. Horizontal: 3 cubits
from the opening, origin and direction unknown.
“[In] the cave of the pillar with the two [en]trances, facing east, [at] the northern entrance, dig
three [cu]bits: there is a jar, in it one scroll; under it 42 talents.”
A pillar, not a terrace. The cave as a whole fronts east; the northern entrance is the northern of
the pair. Three cubits is a depth; the silver lies under the jar.
Atlas: possible only, low; Kh. Qumran and its nearby cliff caves. Comparison caves in the files: Twin
Cave near 11Q (Bar-Adon), Abu Saraj IV/17 and IV/11; none is identified.
IV/17 passes the two-mouth and pillar comparison; mouth bearings, threshold level and date are
unresolved (assessments/entry25_iv17). Twin Cave: both mouths face east; IV/11: an inner pillar only.
